items.title: SAP PaPM Cloud Standard Model: What's New as of 2026-10-06?
items.author: MarijaRistinSremcevic
items.text:
Greetings, SAP Community! 👋 
 We are back with the latest What's New updates for SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Standard Model. This round of improvements covers a lot of ground – and if you work with Joule, Modeling, or Process Management on a regular basis, you will likely feel the difference. 
 Joule keeps growing – it now covers two more application screens. The Properties panel in Modeling opens the moment you select a node. You can delete process run data without removing the instance itself. And notification preferences have gotten a lot more specific. Whether you spend most of your time in Environment , Process Management , or Modeling , this update has something for you. Here is what has changed 📢 

 Joule 
 Joule Now Available in Environment and Process Management 
 Until now, business users could make use of Joule to help them with their reports. With this enhancement, Joule assistance is no longer limited to Report Management. Now Joule also supports the Environment and Process Management applications. 
 Imagine asking Joule about pending process activities, cloning last month's process instance, and checking your environment setup. That is now possible. More than that, Joule in Standard Model can provide information and perform supported actions across all three applications – you don’t need to navigate to a specific application before asking. 
 In the Environment application, Joule can provide information about existing environments and nodes. Use Act mode to create, edit, move, or delete them through conversation. Joule asks for your confirmation before performing irreversible actions such as deletion. 

 In Process Management , Joule covers process templates, instances, activities, parameters, and selections. In Act mode, you can create a new process instance from a template – including custom selections and parameters in a single instruction – or clone an existing instance as the basis for a new run. You can also edit existing process instances and activities. 

 For more information about Joule and its capabilities in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Standard Model, see Joule in Environment and Joule in Process Management in the SAP Help Portal. 
 For a detailed walkthrough and examples, see SAP PaPM Cloud Standard Model – Joule AI Agent: Environment and Process Management Capabilities . 
 Ask Joule What You Can Do and How 
 Finding out what is available on a given screen – and how to use it – often means leaving the application to search the SAP Help Portal manually. That is no longer the case. 
 Joule now draws on built-in documentation from the SAP Help Portal for SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Standard Model. You can ask Joule what actions are available on a screen, how to perform them, and which roles are required – and get step-by-step answers that reference the actual UI elements and flows. 

 Note 
 This capability is currently available for the following applications: 
 Environment 
 Process Management 
 Report Management 
 For more information about Joule and its capabilities in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Standard Model, see Joule in Standard Model in the SAP Help Portal. 
 Track Joule Conversation from Creation to Deletion 
 If you use the Application Monitor or Process Monitor to review system events, you can now identify actions performed on Joule conversations more easily. 
 Three new run types are available: 
 Joule Conversation Creation : Logged when a conversation with Joule is initiated. 
 Joule Conversation Renaming : Logged when a Joule conversation is renamed. 
 Joule Conversation Deletion : Logged when a Joule conversation is deleted. 
 Dedicated run types help you quickly identify and review Joule conversation activities in your monitoring screens. 
 For more information, see Event Status and Run Types , Application Monitor , and Process Monitor in the SAP Help Portal. 

 System - AI Conversation Monitor 
 Review Action Results Directly on the Screen 
 When managing Joule conversations, it is helpful to see the outcome of an action where you perform it. While toast messages provide quick feedback, it is also important to have those actions recorded and available for later review. 
 With this enhancement, the Message Log in the AI Conversation Monitor now displays the results of upload, download, and delete actions, allowing you to review the results directly where the actions are performed. 

 When you need additional details, you can also review the events logged in the Application Monitor . These events are recorded under the following run types: 
 Joule Conversation Upload 
 Joule Conversation Download 
 Joule Conversation Deletion 
 Together, the Message Log and Application Monitor help you review action results and access the corresponding monitoring records when needed. 
 New to the AI Conversation Monitor ? Refer to AI Conversation Monitor in the SAP Help Portal for an overview of the feature, prerequisites, and procedures for the available actions. For more information and an end-to-end scenario, see SAP PaPM Cloud Standard Model: Introducing the AI Conversation Monitor . 

 Modeling 
 Properties Open Automatically in Modeling 
 Imagine you're working through a model and reviewing mappings and configuration settings. As you move between a Model Table , a Calculation function, and Process Templates , accessing its settings requires two separate actions: selecting the node and opening the Properties panel. 
 With this enhancement, the Properties panel opens automatically when you select a node in the Modeling area. Whether you're reviewing a field, updating a parameter, or configuring a function, the relevant settings are available right away. 
 The same behavior applies when you: 
 Add a node from the palette 
 Copy and paste a node 
 Select a node from the modeling search results 
 If the Properties panel is already open, it automatically updates to display the settings of the newly selected node. 
 This makes it easier to review configuration details across connected modeling functions and stay focused on understanding and refining your model. 
 Manage Fields Directly in "From" Rules 
 When configuring the From rules in Join and Model Join functions, you often need to review or adjust how fields are assigned between join rule types. With this enhancement, you can now view and maintain these assignments directly in the Fields section of the Properties panel. 
 This makes it easier to validate the structure of your join results while configuring the model. 

 For more information, see Join Rule Types in the SAP Help Portal. 
 Expand Your Result Model Table Options with Model Table HANA 
 You can now select a Model Table HANA function in the Result Model Table of supported processing functions. 
 Previously, Model Table HANA functions were not available as result model table options. With this enhancement, you can choose a Model Table HANA function as the result destination for Allocation , Calculation , Derivation , Transfer Structure , Join , View , and Iterative View functions. 
 Instead of introducing an additional function to store results, you can define the target table directly in the processing function configuration, giving you more control over how and where your model results are stored. 
 For more information, see Use Model Table HANA as Result Model Table . 

 Process Management 
 Delete Process Data Without Deleting Process Instances 
 Sometimes, you want to remove the results of a process run without removing the process instance itself. For example, you may no longer need the generated data, but you still want to keep the process instance available for monitoring, auditing, or just for future reference. 
 With this enhancement, you can now use the new Delete Process Data action in Process Management to delete process-related data generated by functions assigned to execution activities in one or more selected process instances while the selected instances are retained. 
 The new Delete Process Data action is available in the Edit section of Process Management . 

 Sample Scenario 
 Consider a process instance that has already been run and generated process data. Before using Delete Process Data , the generated process data is available in the system. After the action, the process data generated is deleted, while the process instance remains available in Process Management . 

 Confirmation Before Deletion 

 Before the deletion starts, the system displays a confirmation dialog so you can review and confirm the action. 
 Additional Option for Deleting Process Instances 
 You also have more flexibility when deleting process instances. The enhanced Delete Process Instance action now includes an Also delete associated process data option. 
 This option lets you choose whether to: 
 delete only the selected process instances; or 
 delete both the selected process instances and their associated process data in a single step. 

 For more information, check our SAP Help Portal documentation: 
 Process Management 
 Delete Process Data 
 Delete Process Instance 
 Receive Notifications for Due Activities 
 Keeping track of upcoming activities is important when actions must be completed before a deadline. 
 With this enhancement, you can receive both in-app and email notifications 3 days before an activity's due date and again on the due date itself . The due date is determined based on the activity's end date . 
 Sample In-App Notifications for Due Process Activities 
 Notifications are sent when a process instance is in the Deployed state, and the associated activities have not yet been completed. Both activity performers and reviewers can receive these reminders. Email notifications include a direct link to the relevant activity, allowing you to access the activity and take the required action. 
 This improves the visibility of pending process activities and helps you stay informed about upcoming deadlines. 
 For more information, see Notifications and Dual Control in the SAP Help Portal. 

 User Profile 
 Notification Preferences by Type and Environment 
 Notifications help you stay informed about changes across your environment, but the notifications you want to receive may differ depending on your role and responsibilities. 
 Previously, notification preferences could only be managed by notification channel, allowing you to activate or deactivate In-App and Email notifications. 
 With this enhancement, you can now configure notification preferences for individual notification types when your administrator allows users to manage those settings. 
 There are two parts to the new experience. 
 First, choose your notification types 
 In Notification Types , you can set your in-app and email preferences separately for: 
 Activity changes 
 Process changes 
 Scheduled jobs 
 Team changes 
 Private environment changes 

 Your administrator still determines which settings you can manage. If a setting has been predefined by your administrator, its checkbox is not editable. 
 Second, choose the environment scope 
 In Environments , you can decide where your notification settings apply: 
 All environments 
 Selected environments 
 All environments except the ones you specify 

 Any notification settings configured by your administrator are not affected by the environment settings you choose. 
 Together, these options give you more control over your personal notification preferences while still respecting the settings managed by your administrator. 
 For more information, see: 
 For users: Notifications - Learn how to manage your notification preferences in User Preferences . 
 For administrators: Global Notification Settings - Learn how to configure notification settings at the global level. 
 For a detailed walkthrough: SAP PaPM Cloud Standard Model: Notification Management in User Preferences – Explore an end-to-end example of how user notification prefer

items.title: What is the Impact of an Expired SAP On-premise Maintenance Agreement?
items.author: Claireomalley
items.text:
SAP still allows access to some information after a maintenance agreement has expired. However, certain services are only available with an active support contract. Login to SAP for Me may still be possible after maintenance has expired, with limited functionality.  
 What is still possible: 
 View existing systems and previously assigned licenses 
 Access to old support cases (read-only) - Users can still view and access cases even if the maintenance on the installation is no longer valid, (unless the installation number is deleted). 
 License keys (excluding maintenance certificates) 
 SSCR keys (Developer & Object) 
 Access to Security Notes 
 What is no longer possible: 
 Submitting new support cases to SAP Support 
 Downloading software, patches, legal changes or updates requiring entitlement 
 Access to SAP Notes and Knowledge Base Articles 
 Accessing full SAP support services such as SAP for Me etc. 
 Who should I contact re expired maintenance? 
 You can reach out to your Account Executive as per KBA 2626344 or SAP Order Management (contracts) by e-mailing   sapcontractcenter@sap.com  according to KBA 1660069  for help with the expired contracts topics. 
 How to find out who my Account Executive is? 
 Contact the Customer Interaction Center (CIC) since they can provide this information. There are several ways to contact the Customer Interaction Center (CIC). Be sure to provide the S-user ID, customer number, and customer name, and details of the issue when contacting the CIC team. 
 Go to the  Customer Interaction Center (CIC)  page, and choose one from the various avenues to contact the   Customer Interaction Center (CIC) :  Chat with CIC , Call Us , or by using Webform

items.title: SAP DRC Cloud Edition para NF-e no Brasil: o que mudou em 2026?
items.author: marcoslimaab
items.text:
Em 2026, a SAP apresentou uma importante evolução para os processos de documentos fiscais eletrônicos no Brasil com a disponibilização da nova integração de NF- e no SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition . 
 A mudança vai além de uma atualização tecnológica. O novo modelo faz parte da estratégia da SAP de consolidar a comunicação fiscal eletrônica em uma plataforma cloud global , padronizada e escalável, capaz de suportar diferentes países, documentos, autoridades fiscais e processos de conformidade. Entre os principais objetivos estão a centralização dos serviços, a padronização da arquitetura de integração, a simplificação do onboarding e a disponibilização das futuras inovações do DRC por meio do Cloud Edition. 
 Para clientes que já utilizam os serviços anteriores do SAP DRC para NF- e no Brasil, entretanto, a adoção do Cloud Edition deve ser tratada como uma migração controlada , envolvendo preparação do sistema, SAP Notes, SAP BTP, certificados digitais, tecnologia, recuperação de documentos pendentes, Manifestação do Destinatário, NSU, ativação dos novos switches e planejamento de cutover. 
 Neste artigo apresento as principais mudanças do SAP DRC Cloud Edition para NF- e no Brasil , sua nova arquitetura e, principalmente, os cuidados técnicos que devem ser considerados durante a migração.

items.title: Specification data (AUSP) deleted without change log after AIF error "Error in Buffer: Update failed
items.author: Ramu-Mannava
items.text:
Issue Title : Specification data ( AUSP ) deleted without change log after AIF error "Error in Buffer: Update failed (ESTDF, I)" - S/4HANA 2023 
 Hello experts, 
 We recently upgraded to SAP S/4HANA 2023 (on-premise) and are seeing a critical issue with specification data updated through an inbound interface. 
 Background : 
 An external system sends payloads to SAP through AIF. Each time the interface is triggered, it creates or updates specification data in Specification Management. Interface errors are monitored in /AIF/ERROR. 
 Issue : 
 Whenever the following error appears in AIF, the existing specification data is deleted: 
 Error in Buffer: Update failed (ESTDF, I) 
 Specifically : 
 The value assignment data stored in table AUSP is removed for the affected specifications. 
 The deletion is not recorded in the specification change logs, so there is no audit trail of what was removed. 
 Expected behavior: 
 If the update fails, the existing specification data should stay unchanged, or the whole transaction should roll back cleanly. 
 Questions : 
 Has anyone seen this error lead to data deletion, especially after an upgrade to S/4HANA 2023? 
 Are there any known SAP Notes about the specification buffer, ESTDF, or AUSP deletion in this release? 
 What is the best way to find the root cause: the AIF action logic, the specification API used, or the update or commit handling? 
 Is there a recommended way to recover the deleted data, given that the change log has no record of it? 
 We are treating this as a priority and would appreciate any suggestions. 
 Thank you! 
 Ramu Mannava

items.title: BTP Build Apps- Hands-on R & D with SAP Build Apps, Cloud Connector and Work Zone Integration
items.author: Kiran_R11
items.text:
Hi Everyone, 
 I recently completed extensive hands-on research and prototyping with SAP Build Apps in an SAP BTP Trial environment, integrating low-code frontends with an S/4HANA backend and publishing them to SAP Build Work Zone. 
 I wanted to share my key technical insights and kick off a discussion with community peers on best practices and future roadmaps. 
 Key Areas Explored & Implementation Highlights: 

 S/4HANA & DMS Integration: 

 Configured SAP BTP Destinations via SAP Cloud Connector to connect low-code UI elements to backend services. 

 Monitored DMS (Document Management System) transaction workloads ( CV01N , CV03N ) and user interactions using ST03N and standard DRAW tables. 

 App Delivery & SAP Build Work Zone Integration: 

 Configured application metadata in SAP Build Work Zone Content Manager. 

 Defined custom Semantic Objects and Actions ( Intent Mapping ) to build native-looking Fiori Launchpad tiles for end-user navigation. 

 Environment & Trial Observations: 

 Tested local deployment flows and analyzed trial account boundaries (such some package export restrictions versioning snapshots). 
 Discussion Points for the Community: 

 Transition to SAP Build Code / BAS: Given the evolution of SAP Build Apps towards unified SAP Build Code and SAP Business Application Studio (BAS), what are the recommended migration patterns for existing low-code UI definitions 

 DMS Tracking Best Practices: How are Basis/Technical teams currently auditing non-GUI/HTTP document retrievals coming through Fiori launchpads at scale beyond standard ST03N / SM20 logs? 
 Is there any alternate method for Low code No code in BTP service in free trial 
 Looking forward to hearing thoughts, insights, and suggestions from fellow SAP builders! 
 Best regards, 
 Kiran

items.title: SAP to Acquire TechWolf, Giving Enterprises Evidence-Based View of Work in the Age of AI
items.author: SAP News
items.text:
WALLDORF and GHENT , Belgium — SAP SE (NYSE: SAP) and TechWolf today announced they have entered into an agreement for SAP to acquire TechWolf, provider of a leading AI work intelligence platform. 
 Automate end-to-end processes, drive context-aware decisions and optimize workforce operations at scale 

 Learn how 

 TechWolf gives enterprises a continuously updated view of the work their people do and the skills they have, using its proprietary data model called context graph for work. The acquisition will bring this context graph, along with TechWolf’s AI models and applied AI research team, into SAP, establishing work intelligence as a strategic SAP asset. The deal is expected to close in Q4 2026, subject to usual closing conditions, including regulatory approval. Terms of the deal were not disclosed. 

 TechWolf works from existing HR and business systems that customers connect. It builds its model of the organization at three levels: the work itself, down to the tasks inside a job; the skills people have and apply; and the external labor market. It maps that against the customer’s business strategy, so the leaders responsible for hiring, reskilling and redeployment are working from better information. 

 TechWolf is expected to become an intelligent core of the SAP SuccessFactors portfolio, supporting the company’s talent and work intelligence strategy. TechWolf will power workforce and talent strategies across SAP SuccessFactors, bringing skills mapping, workforce planning and organizational redesign informed by context from across the Autonomous Enterprise. Once the transaction closes, TechWolf and SAP will unify skills and work data to inform HR and business leaders to guide decisions about development, deployment and workforce transformation. 

 “TechWolf’s proprietary context graph for skills and work provides an excellent grounding layer for agent queries regarding work and skills planning and talent management,” said Manoj Swaminathan, president and chief product officer for SAP Autonomous Suite and member of the Extended Board of SAP SE. “This grounding layer perfectly matches our strategy. It makes token usage more efficient, lowers the cost of deploying workforce agents and will make Joule more intelligent in AI-driven HR scenarios such as skills-based hiring, workforce planning and role redesign.” 

 Joint SAP and TechWolf customers using the technology are seeing measurable results from the partnership the two companies have had. Building on that foundation, SAP and TechWolf will jointly co-innovate a concrete set of new AI-powered workforce and skills optimization products to be designed and developed post-close. SAP plans to integrate TechWolf’s solutions to a greater degree, offering customers even better insights and work intelligence to help organizations plan reskilling, internal mobility and hiring. 

 “Organizations everywhere are trying to figure out how AI is reshaping work, and what their workforce needs to look like because of it,” said Andreas De Neve, CEO and co-founder of TechWolf. “We have spent eight years building the evidence layer to answer those questions. It’s always been our mission to connect skills, tasks and work to help employers solve AI transformation, and joining SAP will allow us to extend that mission across a broader set of business context and larger scale. In this next chapter, we plan to build a world-class AI company.” 

 Subject to closing and required consultation, SAP’s current plans are for TechWolf to remain as an independent entity under CEO Andreas De Neve in its Ghent headquarters, with offices in London, New York and San Francisco, and for its platform to remain available to both SAP and non-SAP customers. J.P. Morgan served as exclusive financial advisor to TechWolf.

 TechWolf is a leading applied AI company that helps large enterprises understand how AI is transforming work and what that means for their workforce. Its platform brings together skills, work, and market intelligence, into a single context graph for work ; Its open-source models have been downloaded more than two million times. TechWolf co-exists with systems enterprises already use, including SAP SuccessFactors and non-SAP applications, and connects with AI tools and agents. Customers include HSBC, Atlas Copco Group, GSK, Ericsson, AMD, MetLife, PayPal and Booking.com. The company offers EU and US data-residency, standard encryption, access controls and certifications including ISO/IEC 42001 and ISO/IEC 27001 that support EU AI Act governance and security. items.title: SAP Puts the Autonomous Enterprise to Work
items.author: SAP News
items.text:
Joule Work, Joule Assistants and SAP Business AI Platform help organizations turn business AI into trusted outcomes across every core function. 

 LAS VEGAS — SAP SE (NYSE: SAP) today showcased the Autonomous Enterprise in action at SAP Connect, demonstrating how Joule Work and Joule Assistants generate value for customers across every line of business. 

 “This is a breakthrough moment for business AI,” said Christian Klein, CEO of SAP SE. “The Autonomous Enterprise has arrived. With Joule and SAP Autonomous Suite, built on SAP Business AI Platform, we’re helping organizations like Novartis, Morgan Foods, Nestlé and PwC connect intelligence across every function to deliver trusted business outcomes.” 
 SAP Connect in 2026: Advancing the Autonomous Enterprise 

 Read the innovation news guide 

 At SAP Connect, these customers shared how the Autonomous Enterprise is already driving measurable value across their businesses: 

 “We’ve co-developed and recently launched a pilot of SAP’s Joule Sourcing Assistant,” said Christoph Buerki, Head of Procurement, Novartis. “Our vision is for AI agents to handle the manual heavy lifting, enabling sourcing professionals to focus on strategy, supplier engagement and value creation.” 

 “At Morgan Foods, we’re already putting the pieces in place for agentic adoption, especially through our technical foundation. The biggest shift will be moving from reactive to predictive, where agents can connect demand signals, inventory levels and supplier status faster than ever before,” said Steve Hankins, Chief Financial Officer, Morgan Foods, “Our superpower will come from people on top of agents. Our approximately 1,000 employees are what make our supply chains work—the technology helps make them even better.” 

 “Our SAP S/4HANA transformation across 140 countries is creating a connected digital core with consistent processes, trusted data and greater visibility across markets and functions. With that foundation, Joule and the Accounts Receivable Assistant can automatically prioritize collections work based on risk and business context, recommend the next best action and help our finance teams respond faster to change,” said Luca Dell’Orletta, Global Head IT Innovation & Enterprise Architecture, Nestlé. 

 “In professional services, billing can be one of the more error-prone processes, with accuracy playing an important role in the client experience. SAP’s Billing Assistant brings greater intelligence to this critical process, helping identify potential issues earlier so our people can deliver better client outcomes and build stronger relationships,” said Jill Notz, Chief Accounting Officer, Controller, Business Services Leader, PwC. Building on the success of the Billing Assistant, PwC and SAP are extending their collaboration into new areas of joint AI innovation. 

 SAP’s Autonomous Enterprise Scales Up 

 Joule Work is beginning its customer rollout as a new AI user interface that lets employees interact with SAP solutions in their own language and complete work across SAP and third-party data. Grounded in business context from SAP Knowledge Graph, which maps more than 7 million data fields, Joule provides information users can rely on. At SAP, Joule Work is already live with 110,000 employees, with the company seeing 20% productivity gains across finance, HR and procurement. A select group of customers also is using Joule Work in their business environments. 

 “After 28 years as an SAP customer, partnering with SAP on our AI journey and the Joule Work desktop early adopter program has delivered more momentum in just a few months than we saw in all the years before,” said Peter Wied, Director of Complexity Management, Maschinenfabrik Reinhausen. “What once required up to an hour of manual effort across our SAP S/4HANA environment is now accessible in seconds through natural language—fundamentally changing how our teams interact with business data.” 

 “The dedicated team has been phenomenal. Their proactive communication, focus on accelerating architecture activation, rapid remediation of defects and overall support have enabled us to become Joule ready much sooner than would have been possible had we needed to navigate these challenges on our own,” said Keith Smith, SAP Platform Architect, CONA Services. “The CONA team is excited about the progress made to date and looks forward to exploring and testing Joule’s capabilities in greater depth over the coming months as we continue our adoption journey.” 

 When a query is not enough, Joule Assistants execute operational work directly within business workflows, using established data, authorizations and audit trails. Customers control the level of autonomy. SAP’s approach is also open: through the Agent2Agent protocol, Joule can connect with third-party AI and agents, bringing governed business context into broader AI workflows. 

 At SAP Connect, SAP showcased how these capabilities generate outcomes across SAP Autonomous Suite: 

 In finance, controllers can automate revenue recognition, disclosures and trade compliance, with early deployments of the International Trade Assistant reducing trade classification effort by up to 50%. 

 In supply chain, planners can turn multi-hour disruptions into one-click resolutions across planning, manufacturing and logistics. 

 In HR, leaders can determine the best way to close workforce gaps, while employees can make smarter benefits choices tailored to their needs. 

 In procurement, decision-makers can identify savings opportunities against peer benchmarks and manage the full contingent workforce life cycle. 

 In customer experience, organizations can turn customer engagement into sales opportunities with AI-powered campaigns, quoting and customer workflows. 

 Across industries, SAP is collaborating with customers to apply AI to specialized industry processes, helping organizations in manufacturing, retail, commodity trading and asset-intensive industries improve decision-making, automate routine actions and build more resilient operations. 

 The Platform Powering Business AI You Can Trust 

 SAP Business AI Platform gives organizations one place to build, contextualize and govern AI across SAP and third-party environments. With Joule Studio, business users and developers can build and extend skills and agents from no-code to pro-code workflows, choosing from more than 70 AI models. SAP Business Data Cloud and SAP Knowledge Graph ground those agents in trusted business data and context, helping organizations select the right model for each use case and better manage AI value and consumption. 

 SAP-managed governance helps organizations scale AI with transparency, accountability and control. SAP AI Agent Hub in SAP LeanIX solutions provides a central inventory of enterprise agents, while SAP’s independently ISO/IEC 42001-certified governance architecture supports regulatory requirements, established authorizations and auditable AI operations. 

 To help organizations adopt AI at scale, SAP’s Business Transformation Management portfolio, including SAP Signavio, SAP LeanIX and SAP WalkMe solutions, provides the toolchain to analyze processes, govern applications and agents, and drive adoption across the enterprise. 

 SAP Brings Embedded Payments to Cloud ERP 

 SAP also announced that it is entering the payments market with SAP Pay, powered by Tereina, an SAP company. Embedded directly in SAP Cloud ERP, SAP Pay executes and reconciles payments within the same workflow when an invoice is due, reducing manual file handling and external processing dependencies, while giving customers greater control. 

 Partners Expand the Reach of Autonomous Business 

 SAP is extending the Autonomous Enterprise beyond SAP’s own application portfolio through new partnerships that bring specialized intelligence directly into SAP workflows. 

 A new partnership between SAP and Moody’s Corporation is designed to embed Moody’s supplier risk monitoring data into SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance. This gives procurement teams continuously updated insights into supplier financial health, operational risk and regulatory status at the point of decision. Organizations will be able to move from periodic risk reviews toward continuous monitoring, enabling Joule Agents to flag supplier risk signals and surface alternatives before disruption affects the business. 

 An expanded partnership with ORO Labs brings procurement orchestration to SAP customers as a solution extension. items.title: New AI Features in SAP Enterprise Threat Detection, Cloud Edition
items.author: katrin_karl
items.text:
Security investigations are often complex and time-consuming. Monitoring agents must sift through vast amounts of log data, evaluate the risk posed by individual ABAP objects, and translate technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations. 
 Since August we've introduced three AI-assisted features in SAP Enterprise Threat Detection, cloud edition that help monitoring agents work more efficiently: Behavior analysis, criticality assessments for ABAP objects, and recommendation templates. 
 Let's take a closer look at what's new. 

 Behavior analysis: Let AI surface suspicious activity for you 
 When an investigation is underway and you've identified suspicious users through alerts, the harder question surfaces: what exactly did they do, and how serious was it? Manually reviewing large volumes of log data to answer that takes time you often don't have. 
 That's where behavior analysis comes in. From the Behavior Analysis tab on the investigation details page, you can trigger an AI-powered analysis of the users already linked to your investigation—without leaving your current context. The AI examines their activity across your event data and returns a list of suspicious log events, each tagged with a severity level (Very High, High, Medium, or Low) and an explanation of the AI's reasoning. You can then select individual events and assign them to your investigation as evidence. 
 What you'll need: The UEBAManager role and accepted SAP AI Terms and Conditions 
 For more information, see Running a Behavior Analysis | SAP Help Portal . 

 Criticality information for ABAP objects: Know your risk at a glance 
 Not every ABAP object carries the same risk — but assessing that risk manually takes expertise and time. AI-assisted criticality assessments are now available for four ABAP object types: HTTP paths, function modules, transactions, and reports. 
 The assessment is available directly within the apps where you already work as a monitoring agent: Analyze Log Events , Manage Value Lists , Manage Investigations , and Manage Alerts . When you request criticality information for an object, the system returns: 
 A criticality level (Very High, High, Medium, Low, or Unknown) 
 A plain-language explanation of why the object is security-critical 
 Remediation recommendations to reduce the risk 
 Where applicable, details about relevant SAP Security Notes, including CVSS scores and publication dates 
 A feedback option lets you flag inaccurate or misleading AI-generated content helping improve results over time. 
 What you'll need: The roles CriticalObjectsAIManager and accepted SAP AI Terms and Conditions. 
 For more information, see Criticality Information for ABAP Objects | SAP Help Portal . 

 AI-assisted recommendation templates: Faster, more consistent investigation reports 
 When closing an investigation, monitoring agents write a recommendation for the customer — what happened, why it matters, and what to do next. Getting that right, consistently, across many different patterns, can be a challenge. 
 We've made it easier with AI-assisted recommendation templates. In the Manage Patterns app, you can now use a chat interface to describe the template you need, and the system generates a structured draft. You can then refine it through the chat or edit it directly before saving. 
 Each template follows a clear three-part structure: what happened (investigation result), why it matters (alert reason), and what to do (recommended action). Placeholders in the template are automatically filled with real event data when a monitoring agent generates a recommendation for a specific investigation. 
 You can create templates at two levels: global templates that apply across all tenants, and tenant-specific templates. SAP-provided templates for standard patterns are also available to view as a reference. 
 What you'll need: The roles CriticalObjectsAIManager and CrossTenantCriticalObjectsManager and accepted SAP AI Terms and Conditions. 
 For more information, see Creating Recommendation Templates | SAP Help Portal . 

 Wrapping up 
 These three features reflect a broader direction we're taking with SAP Enterprise Threat Detection: putting AI where it reduces friction in security work. Behavior analysis helps you focus on the activities that matter most. Criticality assessments give you instant context on risky ABAP objects without having to dig through documentation. And AI-assisted recommendation templates help you produce clearer, more consistent reports in less time. 
 Together, these innovations help security teams make better-informed decisions and respond faster to potential threats.

items.title: What’s New in Transportation Management of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 - FP02
items.author: eric_osterroth
items.text:
Today the latest Feature Package 02 (FP02) of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 and SAP S/4HANA 2025 OP was released. 
 The latest innovations in SAP Transportation Management in SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud 2025 Feature Pack 2 highlights many enhancements that improve flexibility, transparency, and external collaboration in Freight Order Management as well as i mprove planning accuracy, usability, and flexibility across transportation processes. . There are quite a number of innovations in the area of clean core that support the clean-core concept and extensibility. 
 Lets first have a look into 
 Freight Order Management 
 Authorization to resolve freight document blocks 
 The first enhancement introduces a new Business Add-In (BAdI) that enables customers to define who is authorized to overrule or delete freight document blocks. Previously, any user with edit authorization could remove planning, execution, or invoicing blocks. With the new enhancement, organizations can implement their own authorization logic—for example, restricting compliance-related block overrides to specific key users—without modifying the standard application. 

 Result of the authorization check implemented in the BAdI 

 Processing and parking of reported external events 
 Another major improvement addresses event reporting from external applications such as SAP Business Network for Logistics or from EWM. 
 Instead of rejecting events that cannot be processed because of missing predecessor events or execution blocks, SAP TM now parks these events and provides clear document errors directly within the freight document. This gives business users full visibility into the issue, allows them to resolve problems without technical message monitoring tools, and automatically reprocesses parked events once blocking conditions have been resolved. 

 Display of parked events and related actions 

 Support of external planning for star-shaped freight orders 
 The third mayor innovation is an enhancement for external planning, which is very important for many customers that let freight orders for instance plan by their carriers for instance in hub based pickup scenarios . SAP TM now fully supports the creation, update, and cancellation of star-shaped freight orders through standard external planning interfaces. This extends existing external planning capabilities to scenarios where detailed routing information remains with the carrier while allowing shippers to benefit from simplified freight order management. The enhancement delivers greater consistency across external planning processes while preserving the specialized behavior of star-shaped freight orders. 
 Enhancements in reporting of greenhouse gas emissions 
 Feature Pack Stack 2 further strengthens Transportation Management's sustainability capabilities by extending the inbound transportation event interface to support the reporting of actual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Carriers can now submit verified emission values and their corresponding units of measure at either the freight order header or individual stage level, providing greater flexibility for real-world emissions reporting. When emissions are reported at the document level, SAP TM transparently distributes the values across stages for analytical purposes while preserving the original reported value at the document level. These enhancements simplify the integration of carrier-provided emissions data and support more accurate sustainability reporting within transportation processes. 
 For more detailed information please have a look at following blog post: Reporting of GHG emissions 
 Emissions reported by the carrier and display in the freight order document 

 Filtering of Product Hierarchies 
 This Feature Pack also introduces new extensibility options that significantly improve how product and package hierarchies are processed during SAP Transportation Management (TM) integration. The new functionality addresses a long-standing challenge in integrated logistics processes, where different applications require different representations of the same business document. 
 Sales kits created in SAP SD are typically expanded into hierarchical item structures. While this level of detail is required for order processing, it is often not the optimal representation for transportation planning or warehouse execution. Depending on the business scenario, TM may only require the top-level kit item, while in other cases only the shippable components are relevant. Similar challenges exist for multi-level package hierarchies. 
 FPS2 introduces new and enhanced Business Add-Ins (BAdIs) that allow customers to control these hierarchy representations in a clean-core compliant manner. A new hierarchy filtering method enables independent filtering of both product and package hierarchies, allowing customers to retain only top-level items, only the lowest-level items, or the complete hierarchy. This filtering is applied within the logistics integration flow, enabling each consuming application to receive the representation that best matches its business requirements. 

 Hierarchy levels can be filtered on different levels based on customer needs 
 The enhancement also covers TM-induced delivery split scenarios. A new BAdI provides the necessary extensibility to adjust hierarchy information before it is transferred back to SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM), ensuring that both systems remain synchronized even when they operate on different hierarchy representations. 
 Beyond improving functional flexibility, the new extensibility helps reduce unnecessary document complexity and data volume, particularly in scenarios involving deeply nested packaging structures. Most importantly, the solution is fully upgrade-safe and clean-core compliant, replacing the implicit enhancements that many customers have relied on in previous releases. 
 With these enhancements, FPS2 provides a standardized and maintainable framework for adapting product and package hierarchy handling to individual business processes while preserving seamless integration between SAP SD, LE, TM, and EWM. 

 Means of Transport and Equipment Type Determination with consistent E2E usage in planning & optimization 
 A major focus is the enhanced Means of Transport (MTR) and Equipment Type Determination , and consitent usage through manual and automatic planning processes. 
 The innovation spans from order management into planning in an E2E manner. 
 With Feature Pack 2, SAP Transportation Management significantly extends the Means of Transport (MTR) determination introduced in FP01. While the original functionality was limited to Transportation Requirement Scheduling (TRS), the new release integrates MTR and equipment type determination consistently across the complete transportation planning process. 
 The key innovation is the introduction of a new condition type that determines not only means of transport and vehicle types, but also equipment types such as container types. This information can now be determined and persisted already on the Freight Unit stage as Preferred Means of Transport and Preferred Equipment Type , providing planning components with consistent guidance throughout the entire planning process. 
 The new functionality closes a long-standing gap between order scheduling and operational transportation planning. Previously, sales order scheduling could produce transportation proposals that were not reproducible during manual or optimizer-based freight unit planning, potentially resulting in inconsistent delivery commitments. Now, manual planning, optimizers, scheduling, default route determination, and load planning all leverage the same transportation preferences and determination logic, ensuring much more consistent planning results. 

 End-To-End usage of Preferred Means of Transport and Preferred Equipment Type 
 Another major enhancement is the seamless propagation of preferred means of transport and equipment types from Freight Units into Freight Orders and Container Units. At the same time, planners retain full flexibility, as automatically determined values remain transparent and can be manually overridden whenever required. 
 The enhanced determination logic has also been integrated into core planning components, including Lane Distance and Duration Determination (LDDD), Embedded Scheduling, the VSR Optimizer, Transportation Proposal, Load Consolidation, and Load Utilization Determination. Depending on the planning component, the system either consumes persisted preferred values or dynamically executes the determination at runtime. This enables planning decisions to consider transportation constraints much earlier while reducing the solution space for optimization algorithms and improving planning efficiency. 
 To support these capabilities, the Transportation Cockpit has been enhanced with new fields displaying preferred means of transport, equipment types, their origin, and editing capabilities. In addition, planning profiles now offer a dedicated configuration for the new determination logic. It is also recommended adopting the new equipment type condition type for new implementations, as it provides greater flexibility and is intended to replace the previous vehicle type determination approach over time. 
 Overall a much more comprehensive, rule-based transportation planning concept is introduced. By making transportation and equipment preferences available throughout the planning lifecycle, SAP TM delivers more consistent planning results, improved optimizer performance, greater transparency for planners, and better alignment between sales order scheduling and transportation execution. 

 Now lets have a look into the innovations that are introduced in other area's of 
 Planning & Network 
 Transportation Management continues to enhance planning capabilities with a strong focus on automation, planning accuracy, and flexibility. The latest innovations span Freight Unit Building, Unified Package Building, Load Planning, and Capacity Planning, helping customers model increasingly complex logistics scenarios while reducing implementation effort and the need for custom enhancements. 
 The release delivers important improvements in scheduling . As an example the Appointment validation has been corrected to provide more accurate error messages, and loading and unloading activities must now be scheduled completely within the appointment window instead of only partially overlapping. These changes help create more realistic and reliable transportation schedules.

 Scheduling Result takes into account appointments 
 In addition, the Explain Scheduling Results app has received usability enhancements, including a more efficient grid-based table and the ability to open detailed scheduling analyses in separate browser tabs. 

 More Accurate Freight Unit Building 
 Freight Unit Building now applies an improved packing heuristic based on the First Fit Decreasing algorithm. Compared to the previously used approach, the new heuristic achieves better capacity utilization by reducing unused space within freight units. As a result, fewer freight units are created while overall planning quality improves. An additional benefit is improved runtime performance, making Freight Unit Building both more efficient and more scalable for large planning scenarios.

items.title: Reusable Views on Classification and Lookup Table for SAP Commissions Implementation
items.author: rudrakumar_puppala
items.text:
Lookup tables are stored in fragments. What a compensation analyst sees as a single readable row — "100,000 - 200,000 → 8%" — is physically spread across three or four tables (cs_relationalmdlt, CS_MDLTcell, cs_mdltindex), with separate columns used depending on whether the dimension value is a number, a string, or a date. Writing the SQL to reconstruct that row correctly takes time and is easy to get wrong. 
 Classifiers come in four distinct types. A classifier in SAP Commissions can be a Product (cs_product), a Customer (cs_customer), a Postal Code (cs_postalcode), or a Generic Classifier (cs_genericclassifier). Business users think of these as one concept — "the things in my category tree" — but they are stored in entirely separate tables. Any unified report requires a UNION of all four. 
 Effective dating and soft deletes are everywhere. Every record carries an effectivestartdate, an effectiveenddate, and a removedate. Miss any one of these on any one join and your numbers silently include expired or deleted records. This is the single biggest source of subtle reporting bugs across implementations. 
 Human-readable names hide behind internal keys. Unit types, business units, and processing units are stored as numeric foreign keys (businessunitmap, processingunitseq). Every useful report needs to resolve those into names, which adds more joins and more surface area for mistakes.

Dear SAP QM Team, 
 We need your expert clarification regarding the behavior of Movement Type 321 (Quality Inspection Stock to Unrestricted Use) in our SAP system for all materials were inspection type is active. 
 Scenario 
 Material is configured with Inspection Type 04 (GR from Production) . 
 Upon Goods Receipt from Process Order: 
 Stock is posted to Quality Inspection (QI) stock. 
 Inspection Lot is generated automatically.

 REL CALC SPRQ indicating that the inspection is still active and no Usage Decision has been made.

 Result Recording (QA32/QE51N) 
 Usage Decision (QA11/QA32)

 Inventory moves to Unrestricted Use. 
 The inspection lot remains open in REL status.

 Clarifications Required 
 Is this standard SAP behavior for Movement Type 321? 
 What configuration settings control whether 321 movements are permitted when an open inspection lot exists? 
 Are there any QM-specific settings in: 
 Material Master (QM View) 
 Inspection Type 04 
 Movement Type 321 (OMJJ) 
 Inspection Lot Origin settings that should prevent this stock transfer?

 We would appreciate your guidance on the exact controls and configuration points that govern this behavior.

digest.headline: Thin day: RAP hybrid managed/unmanaged-save PO question, a BAPI silent-failure case, and Public Cloud extensibility gaps dominate community questions.
digest.overview:
Today's material is almost entirely community Q&A with no answers attached. The most useful for ABAP trainers are a RAP question on a managed BO with unmanaged save that creates purchase requisitions and now purchase orders (ref 34), a BAPI_BUPA_ROLE_ADD_2 call that returns no error but does not add the customer role (ref 58), and a Fiori Elements question on multi-select in object page tables (ref 93). Only one item is a technical how-to: a Cloud Connector 2.16.2 install guide on SLES 15 SP6 (ref 53).

The pattern is that developers are hitting extension-point and data-availability limits. This shows in Public Cloud BAdI and function-module gaps (refs 65, 88) and in on-premise output and BAdI hooks that don't expose the data needed (ref 97). Note that the source summaries contain inferences not stated in the posts. Treat claims about solutions as unverified unless the post itself gives them.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Silent BAPI failures are a classic trap. Common causes to check are the RETURN table contents, a missing BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT, and whether the customer role needs more data than the BAPI supplies in S/4. The post itself does not give a root cause.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Selection behaviour and action binding in Fiori Elements are driven by metadata and manifest settings plus the RAP action definition. Developers often look in the wrong layer.

top_stories.why_it_matters: These show the cost of moving classic custom code to Public Cloud. Teach students to inventory exits and BTEs before migration and to check released extension points.

deep_dives.title: Managed RAP with unmanaged save orchestrating standard BOs
deep_dives.explanation:
The question in ref 34 uses a custom managed BO with `with unmanaged save`. A determination calls `MODIFY ENTITIES OF i_purchaserequisitiontp` to create purchase requisitions, using `%cid` and `%cid_ref` to link header and items. A custom table `zpr_request` stores the mapping.

The same technique applies to `i_purchaseordertp` if that interface is available in your release. Check the released BDEF and its supported operations. A PO needs a supplier, purchasing organisation and so on, so the input mapping and the standard validations will differ from a PR. These details come from general RAP knowledge, not from the post.

Points to teach: `%cid` is a temporary key valid within one request. After the call, `%pid`/`%tky` and CONVERT KEY (as used in the post) map to the final keys. Handle `failed` and `reported` from the called BO, and be careful about where in the RAP interaction/save phase you call another BO's MODIFY, because the save sequence has restrictions on modifying and committing. Test this on your own system.

deep_dives.title: Silent BAPI success: verifying BAPI_BUPA_ROLE_ADD_2 in S/4
deep_dives.explanation:
In ref 58, BAPI_BUPA_CREATE_FROM_DATA creates a partner and BAPI_BUPA_ROLE_ADD_2 with FLCU01 returns without error, yet BP does not show the role. The post gives no cause.

A systematic check: read the whole RETURN table, including warning and info types, not just type E. Confirm BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT runs after the sequence, and that the partner is committed before the role call. Then check the database tables for the role directly (BUT100) to separate display problems from persistence problems. Also check whether customer data in S/4 requires the CVI link and further customer-specific data. That last point is general S/4 knowledge, not stated in the post.

A robust pattern is to wrap the calls, collect all messages, and read the partner back after commit. For larger migrations, consider the released BP APIs or the BP maintenance classes rather than old BAPIs.

deep_dives.title: Fiori Elements multi-select on object page tables for RAP actions
deep_dives.explanation:
Ref 93 asks how to replace radio buttons with checkboxes for line items so that approve/reject runs on selected items only. The post does not name a solution.

In Fiori Elements, table selection mode is typically set in the app's manifest.json table settings, not in the RAP behavior definition. Actions are exposed through `@UI.lineItem` entries of type `#FOR_ACTION` on the child entity. For the action to run per selected row, define it as an instance action on the child entity in the behavior definition. This is general Fiori Elements/RAP knowledge, so verify it on your release.

Teaching exercise: compare what happens when the action is defined on the header versus the item, and how selected keys arrive in `keys` in the action implementation.

post_drafts.text:
*BAPI returned no error, but the role is not there.*

A community case: BAPI_BUPA_CREATE_FROM_DATA, then BAPI_BUPA_ROLE_ADD_2 with FLCU01. No error, but the customer role is missing in BP.

3. Read the partner back after commit

interview_questions.question: A BAPI_BUPA_ROLE_ADD_2 call returns no error, but the customer role FLCU01 does not appear in transaction BP. How do you investigate?
interview_questions.answer: First I read the complete RETURN table, including warnings and information messages, because success can hide messages. Then I check that BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT is executed after the partner creation and the role call, since the BAPIs do not commit by themselves. I verify persistence by reading the partner back in a new LUW and checking table BUT100. I also consider whether the customer role in S/4 needs additional data, such as the customer-vendor integration link. I would build a wrapper that collects all messages and fails the batch record when the read-back does not show the role. For larger migrations I would compare with the released BP APIs.

interview_questions.question: In a managed RAP BO with unmanaged save, how do you create a purchase requisition through a released standard BO, and what pitfalls apply when extending that to purchase orders?
interview_questions.answer: You use MODIFY ENTITIES OF the released BDEF, passing the create data with %cid for new instances and %cid_ref to link child items to the header. After the call you evaluate failed and reported, and map temporary keys to the final keys with CONVERT KEY or the %pid/%tky handling, then persist the mapping in your own table. For purchase orders, first check that a released interface exists in your release and which operations it supports. PO data requirements differ, for example the supplier is required, and the standard BO runs its own validations. You must also respect the RAP save-sequence restrictions on where such calls and commits are allowed. I would test the sequence thoroughly, including failure handling, before relying on it.

interview_questions.question: A customer is moving from S/4HANA on-premise to Public Cloud and relies on BTEs and function modules for custom logic. How do you approach it?
interview_questions.answer: I start with an inventory of all custom code and exits, and classify each by business purpose. For each, I check whether a released extension point, key-user extensibility, or a developer extensibility option in Public Cloud exists. Where none exists, as seen in the payment advice case and the CO11N validation case, I look at process alternatives such as configuration, output or form settings, or side-by-side extensions on BTP. I bring those gaps to the project early as scope and cost items. I do not promise to recreate the classic code. Sometimes a business process change is the correct answer.
